land.text: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture was succeeded by the Painted Grey Ware culture (infobox 'followed by: Black and red ware, Painted Grey Ware culture')

successors.note: OCP ends in -1500 on the infobox and Painted Grey Ware starts in -1200; Uesugi dates the OCP to c. 1900-1300 BCE, which would close the gap. The black and red ware is not a dossier of this group.

correction.text: north-eastern Rajasthan, where 'early characteristic ceramics near Jodhpura (Jaipur district)' date to the 3rd millennium and the Sahibi valley sites lie; the Haryana and Punjab sites of the same culture are left to the Indus dossier (sa-01-a), which draws the Late Harappan Haryana, Punjab and Delhi to -1300

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no OCP row). Infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE', 'generally dated 2000-1500 BCE'. The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 37,000 km2. Before the Gangetic plain: Jodhpura and the Sahibi sites in the Aravalli foothills.

correction.text: 'from eastern Punjab to northeastern Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh': the Ganges-Yamuna Doab (Hastinapur, Sinauli, Bahadrabad, Hulas, Bargaon, Jhinjhana, Kausambi, Ahichchhatra) added to north-eastern Rajasthan; Haryana, the Indian Punjab and Delhi (Mitathal, Katpalon, Red Fort) stay with the Indus dossier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The culture reached the Gangetic plain in the early 2nd millennium BCE'; Uesugi dates the culture c. 1900-1300 BCE; the Copper Hoard page (second page) puts the hoards, 'mainly in the western Ganges-Yamuna doab', in the first half of the 2nd millennium BCE. The shape resolves to about 165,000 km2; the page names sites and rivers, not a boundary.

region.text: north-eastern Rajasthan, where 'early characteristic ceramics near Jodhpura (Jaipur district)' date to the 3rd millennium and the Sahibi valley sites lie; the Haryana and Punjab sites of the same culture are left to the Indus dossier (sa-01-a), which draws the Late Harappan Haryana, Punjab and Delhi to -1300

ledger.note: c. 2000 BCE: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture appears in north-eastern Rajasthan and along the Sahibi river. Infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE'; 'Early characteristic ceramics near Jodhpura (Jaipur district, Rajasthan) date to the 3rd millennium'; sites lie 'along the Sahibi River and its tributaries, the Krishnavati and Soti'. The year is the infobox's; the region is my reading of the named sites.

region.text: the Ganges-Yamuna Doab and western Uttar Pradesh: 'the culture extended across the Indo-Gangetic Plain, from eastern Punjab to northeastern Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh'

ledger.note: c. 1900 BCE: the culture reaches the Gangetic plain. The page says only 'the early 2nd millennium BCE' for this and Uesugi's c. 1900-1300 BCE for the culture; -1900 is my bridging year. The Copper Hoard page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper_Hoard_culture) puts the hoards 'mainly in the western Ganges-Yamuna doab' in 'the first half of the 2nd millennium BCE'.

region.text: the OCP country of the Doab and north-eastern Rajasthan

ledger.note: c. 1500 BCE: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture ends and gives way to the Painted Grey Ware culture. Infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE'; the page says it was succeeded by Painted Grey Ware (the infobox also lists Black and red ware as a successor, the body Northern Black Polished Ware).

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from villages and copper hoards ('most sites are small, densely distributed villages'), not from frontiers.

sources.title: Ochre Coloured Pottery culture
sources.note: Identity, infobox 2000-1500 BCE, Uesugi 1900-1300, range 'from eastern Punjab to northeastern Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh', Sahibi sites, Jodhpura, relation to the Late Harappan and Painted Grey Ware.

sources.title: Copper Hoard culture
sources.note: Dating of the hoards to the first half of the 2nd millennium BCE and their link to OCP; the page has no infobox.

notes: Type culture although the schema describes cultures before 3400 BCE: the Indus dossier (sa-01-a) uses the same convention to -1300. The page gives no area and there is no Cliopatria row, so no area check was possible. Overlap with the Indus dossier: the OCP page puts the culture in eastern Punjab and Haryana (Mitathal, Katpalon, the Sahibi in Mahendragarh) and shows 'similarities with the Late Harappan culture' (Uesugi: 'a Late Harappan expansion'; Kumar: 'a contemporary neighbour'). Haryana, the Indian Punjab and Delhi 80 km are drawn by indus-valley-civilization to -1300, so they are subtracted here; a gap-filler may prefer to give them to this culture. Chronology: the infobox 2000-1500 leaves -1499..-1201 between OCP and Painted Grey Ware (infobox 1200) as nobody's land; Uesugi's c. 1900-1300 and PGW 'from 1300' would close it. The Ahichchhatra, Hastinapur and Kausambi sites reappear in the Painted Grey Ware dossier.
